item.title: Accelerated Global MPPT Under Partial Shading: A Physics-Regularized I-V Search With Logistic Modeling and Search Space Exclusion
item.description: Partial shading conditions in photovoltaic (PV) systems generate complex multipeak power-voltage characteristics that challenge conventional maximum power point tracking (MPPT) algorithms. While metaheuristic approaches offer global search capabilities, they often entail high computational costs, extensive hyperparameter tuning, and issues with stochastic convergence. This article proposes a deterministic, parameter-free global MPPT (GMPPT) strategy termed physics-regularized I–V search with logistic modeling (PRISM). The proposed method uses a novel logistic estimator that reconstructs the PV I–V curve from a minimal number of operating points, eliminating the need for irradiance or temperature sensors. By integrating this estimator with a physics-aware case classifier and a constrained best-first branch-and-bound search, the algorithm efficiently prunes suboptimal search regions, ensuring convergence to the global maximum. Experimental validation demonstrates that PRISM significantly reduces tracking time compared to state-of-the-art metaheuristics and eliminates the need for random parameter initialization. Under partial shading, the method achieved an average tracking time of 0.45 s with 99.90% steady-state efficiency, while under uniform conditions it achieved 0.40 s and 99.92% efficiency, providing a robust, low-computational-burden solution for real-time applications under dynamic environmental conditions.

item.title: Synchronization Stability of Microgrids Considering the Interaction Between GFL and AHO Inverters Under Current Limits
item.description: Microgrids composed of grid-following and grid-forming inverters based on the Andronov-Hopf Oscillator (AHO) are becoming increasingly popular. However, when grid voltage drops, AHO inverters may enter the current-limiting mode, which complicates the synchronization stability. To solve this challenge, this letter establishes a dynamic power angle model to describe the synchronization behavior of the microgrid under current limits. Equivalent power surfaces are defined to analyze the stability mechanism, and the effects of various parameters on the synchronization stability are clarified. Then, a stabilization control strategy is proposed, and the impact of control parameters on the region of attraction of the controlled system is analyzed. Finally, hardware-in-the-loop tests are conducted to verify the effectiveness of the proposed analysis and stability enhancement strategy.

item.title: Physics-Priori Neural Converters Modeling for Intelligent EMT Simulation
item.description: This letter proposes a physics-priori neural converter model based on port-Hamiltonian neural ordinary differential equations for real-time, high-fidelity, and stable electromagnetic transient simulation. By preserving the switching-induced interconnection topology and learning only uncertain dissipation and physical parameters, the model improves physical consistency and ensures bounded recursive AI-integrated simulation. Real-time simulation and hardware experiment tests verify that the proposed model supports parameter correction, achieves fast execution, and provides higher accuracy than other AI methods.

item.title: Nonresonant Soft-Switching Flyback Converter
item.description: Resonant spikes increase the voltage and current stress across semiconductors in resonant converters, and the nonresonant zero-voltage-switching flyback converter requires five switches. To address these issues, a nonresonant zero-current-switching (ZCS) flyback converter is proposed. The proposed converter has only one switch, which exhibits lower voltage stress than existing flyback converters. It employs pulse-width modulation control, enabling nonresonant ZCS turn-on of the switch over all duty cycles and load conditions. All diodes also achieve nonresonant ZCS. Finally, an experimental prototype verifies the feasibility of the proposed converter.

item.title: Fast and Accurate Core-Loss Measurement Using Twin Transformers With Dynamic Phase-Error Compensation
item.description: This letter presents a magnetic core-loss measurement technique under quasi-sinusoidal excitation that exploits naturally damped oscillations, eliminating the need for costly radio-frequency (RF) power amplifiers and their associated flux-driving limitations. A half-bridge series-resonant circuit excites the core under test (CUT) to a targeted flux density through forced oscillation, after which core-losses are extracted from the subsequent natural decay, enabling wide-range loss measurement from a single transient event. To ensure high accuracy, a dynamic phase-error compensation algorithm is introduced that corrects cycle-by-cycle voltage–current phase misalignment using a reference air-core transformer with an identical physical structure to the CUT. Experimental results from 100 to 1000 kHz show close agreement with steady-state RF amplifier-based benchmark measurements while achieving over 15× faster measurement speed.

item.title: An Arm-Inductor-Less Modular Alternate Supporting Converter With Reduced Submodule Capacitance
item.description: The modular multilevel converter (MMC) is the mainstream high-voltage direct current transmission topology, but massive submodule (SM) capacitors and bulky arm inductors severely constrain its power density. To overcome these limitations, this letter proposes the modular alternate supporting converter (MASC). The three-phase legs of MASC alternately support the DC bus, while the remaining arms switch between conducting and blocking states. This unique operation naturally eradicates interphase commutation, achieving an inductor-less architecture while retaining pure modularity. Concurrently, by inherently suppressing low-frequency power fluctuations, the proposed MASC reduces SM capacitance requirements by approximately 40% compared to conventional HB-MMCs, thereby yielding a 1.41-fold increase in overall power density. Experimental results validate the MASC topology for lightweight converter designs.

item.title: A Dummy-Free Low-Power LDO With Sub-1-$\mu $A Quiescent Current for Fast Wake-Up in Long-Term Standby Applications
item.description: This letter presents a dummy-free and low-power low-dropout regulator (LDO) designed for long-term standby applications. The proposed LDO eliminates the conventional dummy current by using an error amplifier-based biasing scheme, significantly reducing standby power consumption. To further enhance transient response under low quiescent current (IQS) conditions, a modified buffer adaptively adjusts its bias current, and a slew-rate enhancer operates without any static current. The LDO exhibits less than 70 mV undershoot for 0–140 mA load steps with sub-1-μA IQS.

item.title: Quantitative Analysis of Transient Synchronization Stability for Grid-Forming Converters Under Asymmetrical Faults
item.description: The transient synchronization stability (TSS) of grid-forming converters (GFMCs) under symmetrical faults has been extensively investigated. However, quantitative TSS analysis under asymmetrical faults—the most frequently encountered fault type in practice—remains largely unexplored. To bridge this gap, this letter proposes a region of attraction estimation method for the GFMC under asymmetrical faults and further quantitatively evaluates the impact of negative-sequence (NS) current injection required by existing grid codes on TSS. It is shown that the sequence coupling induced by NS current injection reduces the positive-sequence electromagnetic output power and contracts the stability boundary, thereby degrading TSS. This reveals a tradeoff in GFMC operation under asymmetrical conditions: NS current injection mitigates voltage unbalance but increases the risk of instability.

item.title: Dispatch of Inertia and Damping for Multiconverter Oscillation Mitigation
item.description: In power-electronics-dominated power systems, virtual inertia and damping are commonly designed according to low-frequency security and stability requirements. This article shows that, even under the same total inertia and damping budgets, different spatial allocations can lead to distinct mid-frequency oscillatory fragilities. To capture this effect, a band-limited joint frequency–power worst-case amplification metric is formulated. A fixed-budget inertia–damping reallocation method is then proposed: it first constructs a safety-feasible baseline and then redistributes the same total inertia and damping to suppress the dominant amplification peak in the target frequency band. Simulation and hardware results show that the proposed reallocation reduces the system-wide joint frequency–power amplification without increasing total control resources.

item.title: Neural Network Based On-Time Control of Boundary Conduction Mode Boost Power Factor Corrector
item.description: Additional on-time control in boundary conduction mode (BCM) boost power factor correction (PFC) circuits has been a practical solution to improve power quality. However, optimal on-time profiles are difficult to obtain using conventional model-based approaches due to nonlinearities in both hardware and control. These nonlinearities require extensive analytical modeling, parameter extraction, and tuning, which leads to a complex development process. Data-driven on-time control can estimate accurate on-time without analytical modeling because it inherently includes hardware nonlinearities. However, conventional approximation methods, such as lookup tables and polynomial fitting have limitations in terms of memory requirement and computation time. Although artificial intelligence (AI)-based methods have recently been used in power-electronics applications to reduce the burden of model analysis and optimize, the application of AI to additional on-time control in BCM boost PFC converters remain limited. This article proposes a lightweight neural network (NN)-based on-time control method using pretrained NN, without requiring analytical modeling. A complete design flow—data collection, training, and real-time deployment—is presented. Since the proposed NN can be rapidly retrained with newly collected data, it can be easily adapted to different device selections or circuit parameter variations without extensive redesign effort. Experimental results from a prototype with 110–220 VRMS input and 400 V/150 W output validate the effectiveness of the proposed NN controller in achieving competitive performance in terms of power factor and total harmonic distortion of the input current with the real time application on a low-cost microcontroller unit.

item.title: High-Power Four-Port Converters With Integrated Storage for Fast and Slow EV Charging
item.description: This article presents two isolated four-port converters for high-power electric vehicle (EV) fast-charging applications. One converter is based on fully processed power conversion (FPPC), while the other adopts partial power processing (PPPC). By utilizing both FPPC and PPPC configurations, the proposed design achieves a reduction in size and cost. In addition, the PPPC configuration allows partial power to flow directly from the energy storage system to the EV, further reducing cost by lowering the converter rating, minimizing losses, and improving efficiency. The article also addresses internal coupling challenges in multiport systems by introducing a dual decoupling approach, which combines hardware-based impedance design with software-level control using frequency and phase shift modulation. Detailed mathematical modeling for power flow analysis, along with thermal and reliability analysis, is provided to evaluate performance. The proposed converters are validated through simulation, and a laboratory prototype of 1 kW is used to confirm the effectiveness of the proposed converter design. The PPPC configuration achieves a peak efficiency of 98.1%.

item.title: Coupled-Transformer Voltage Regulator With Integrated Magnetics and High Power Density
item.description: This article proposes a high-power-density flux-split coupled-transformer voltage regulator (FS-CTVR) with improved dynamic response for 48 V data center power supplies. The topology resolves the large winding loss and insufficient dynamic performance of convenitional current Doubler rectifier (CDR) converters. A magnetically integrated transformer with primary flux splitting and secondary parallel current sharing is developed to achieve a high turns ratio, reduce winding footprint and current stress, and mitigate winding losses. Additional PCB winding layers form a common coupling loop for multiphase CDR transformers, which reduces transient output inductance and improves dynamic response. Comprehensive analysis, design and performance evaluation of the FS-CTVR are presented. A two-module parallel prototype (54 V input, 0.9 V output) is built and tested. Each module delivers 150 A full-load current, 88.6% full-load efficiency and 1687 W/in3 power density, with a dynamic voltage fluctuation of 88 mV. Experimental results validate the feasibility and superior performance of the proposed topology.

item.title: Buck–Boost ZVqZCS Control for DAB Converters in 7.2 kW GaN-Based OBC Applications
item.description: This article presents a novel buck-boost zero voltage quasi-zero current switching (ZVqZCS) approach for nonresonant isolated dual active bridge (DAB) converters. The mathematical principle of the proposed control strategy is developed to ensure full zero voltage switching (ZVS) and 75% (six out of eight switches) quasi-zero current switching (qZCS) across a broad range of input and output voltages necessary for bidirectional onboard chargers. The primary control variables are the switching frequency (fast loop) and the reference voltage of power factor correction circuit (slow loop). A phase-shift variable is introduced to ensure ZVS with qZCS at the minimum feasible current, thereby minimizing turn-off and dead-time losses. The proposed buck-boost ZVqZCS scheme is implemented in both charging and discharging modes, considering constant-current, constant-power, and constant-voltage operations in charging mode. The inverse/backflow power is minimized without complex optimization, and the di/dt of power loops is reduced to nearly half of the conventional approaches. The design procedure for active and passive components in the proposed approach is introduced. Burst mode is utilized to achieve light-load soft switching with ZVqZCS. The result of the proposed method is demonstrated through extensive simulations and experimentally verified and compared with complex DAB modulations on a compact GaN-based 7.2 kW DAB converter.

item.title: An Oscillation-Free Active Gate Driver With Self-Adaptive Overshoot Control for SiC MOSFETs
item.description: Compared with silicon-based metal-oxide-semiconductor field-effect transistors (mosfets), silicon carbide (SiC) mosfets enable higher efficiency and power density in power converters owing to their fast switching capability and high operating frequency. However, the parasitic inductances in the power loop introduce severe voltage overshoot and oscillations during the turn-off transient, degrading device reliability and generating significant electromagnetic interference (EMI). To address these challenges, this article proposes an active gate driver (AGD) that achieves oscillation-free turn-off, along with a self-adaptive overshoot control strategy. By dynamically regulating the gate current profile, the proposed strategy enables precise adjustment of the overshoot voltage to a predefined range, ensuring stable and reliable operation under varying conditions. A comprehensive experimental platform is established to validate the proposed approach. Three distinct types of SiC mosfets are evaluated under operating conditions of 600 V/50 A, 100 A, and 200 A, respectively. In addition, a dynamic load variation from 600 V/50 A to 600 V/200 A is conducted to further assess the robustness of the proposed strategy. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed AGD effectively suppresses voltage overshoot and eliminates oscillations while maintaining stable switching characteristics. Furthermore, the self-adaptive control strategy enables cycle-by-cycle regulation, achieving robust and oscillation-free operation across a wide range of operating conditions.

item.title: A Localized Jet Microchannel Heatsink With Enhanced Thermal Performance for High-Capacity SiC Power Modules
item.description: With the refinement of processes and maturation of technology, high-capacity silicon carbide (SiC) power modules are becoming core components driving the advancement of new energy, offshore wind power, and new-type power systems. However, as the voltage and current ratings of SiC power modules continue to increase, their power density rises significantly, and the heat flux density intensifies sharply, imposing higher demands on the performance of the heatsink. To address this, this article proposes a localized jet microchannel (LJMC) heatsink suitable for high-capacity SiC power modules, analyzes its structural advantages over traditional manifold microchannel heatsink, and optimizes its design using an automatic heatsink optimization algorithm developed in prior research. Furthermore, experimental validation of the LJMC heatsink is conducted using a 3.3 kV/2000 A SiC power module as a test subject. The results show that, under the same pumping power, the optimized LJMC heatsink reduces processing costs by 13.3%, improves thermal uniformity by 42.0%, and lowers thermal resistance by 9.8% compared to a traditional Pin-Fin heatsink.

item.title: Power Electronic Converter on Bio-Based Substrate: Design, Characterization, Aging, and Disassembly
item.description: To mitigate the environmental impact of e-waste in power electronics, this article introduces a bio-based insulated metal substrate (B2IMS) consisting of polylactic acid (PLA) deposited on a metal plate. The proposed substrate addresses two major limitations of PLA-based substrates for power converters: it remains effective under cyclic operating temperatures exceeding 100 °C, and it is compatible with environmentally friendly SnAgCu solder, which requires a reflow temperature of 249 °C. The article describes the fabrication of a 35 W buck converter using the B2IMS and evaluates its performance under repetitive operating temperatures above 100 °C. Despite the low glass-transition temperature of PLA, the converter demonstrates stable operation during active power cycling. Finally, PLA hydrolysis is used for converter disassembly, thereby optimizing recycling selectivity and maximizing material valorization potential. These results represent a critical step toward the deployment of more environmentally sustainable power converters. This article is accompanied by a video file demonstrating the hydrolysis-based disassembly of the bio-based substrate part of the power electronics converter.

item.title: Influence of Packaging Technologies on Pulsed Power Capability of SiC MOSFETs Across Different Timescales
item.description: The pulsed power capability of SiC mosfets under extreme operating conditions (e.g., short circuits, surge currents) is critical to the robustness of power conversion systems. Packaging influences the transient thermal impedance and chip temperature rise, thereby impacting the device’s pulsed power capability. Therefore, this article investigates the influence of packaging technologies on device pulsed power capability across different timescales. It is found that packaging technologies have little impact on the devices’ short-circuit capability but can affect their surge-current capability. Different package layers influence the devices’ surge current capability across different timescales. For pulsewidths (tp) on the order of hundreds of microseconds, adopting a die top system (DTS) or a copper-clip (Clip) structure on the top surface of the chip can improve the pulsed power capability. The Clip further outperforms the DTS at millisecond timescales due to its larger thermal capacitance. Regarding the bottom die-attach interface, using silver sintering to increase the thermal conductivity enhances the device’s pulsed power capability only as tp approaches 1 ms. Modifying the thermal capacitance or thermal resistance of the direct bonded copper (DBC) affects the chip temperature rise only as tp approaches 10 ms. Moreover, since the DBC is located relatively far from the chip, the resulting reduction in temperature rise is insufficient to improve the pulsed power capability. These findings provide guidelines for package design to improve the pulsed power robustness of SiC devices.

item.title: Breaking SOA Barrier in IGCTs: Extending Turn-Off Capability via Novel Avalanche Controlled Driving Scheme
item.description: The insufficient turn-off current capability is one of the critical obstacles preventing Integrated Gate Commutated Thyristor from wider use in high-power applications. To break through the bottleneck, in this article, a novel boost driving scheme based on the controlled avalanche of the gate–cathode junction is proposed. Based on the scheme, an optimal driving parameter design methodology for the gate driver ensuring thermal and electrical stability is presented. With the developed prototype, the avalanche stability, avalanche reliability, and most importantly turn-off current capability of the proposed scheme are verified with experiments. The results show that more than 46% improvement in turnoff current capability can be achieved through a novel avalanche control scheme.

item.title: An Active Neutral Point Balancing Method With Minimized Harmonic Emission for 3-L NPC Converters
item.description: Neutral-point (NP) voltage regulation is essential for ensuring the safe and reliable operation of three-level neutral-point-clamped converters. When the NP voltage becomes unbalanced, the converter may suffer from distorted modulation signals and increased even-order harmonic emissions. Meanwhile, the intrinsic self-balancing capability weakens as the output power increases, and existing active balancing methods often exhibit limited power-factor adaptability or introduce additional harmonic currents. This article establishes a unified impedance-based model that reveals the NP self-balancing mechanism, characterizes its associated harmonic emission behavior, and explains the loss of balancing capability under high-power conditions. Based on this model, the harmonic behaviors and power-factor limitations of conventional balancing methods are also systematically analyzed. To address these issues, a minimum harmonic emission (MHE) balancing method is proposed by adaptively injecting corrected absolute modulation-wave components through coordinated DC and even-order harmonic channels. The method maintains NP voltage balance over the entire power-factor range while minimizing even-order harmonic emissions across mainstream carrier-based pulsewidth modulation schemes without introducing additional switching losses. Experimental results verify the accuracy of the balancing model and the effectiveness of the proposed method across the full power-factor range through comparative evaluation.

item.title: Robust Sensorless Strategy Based on Dual Extended State Observer Without Fault Localization for Open-Phase Faults in Dual Three-Phase SPMSM Drives
item.description: Dual three-phase surface-mounted permanent magnet synchronous motor (SPMSM) are widely used in various high-reliability applications owing to their high power conversion capability and excellent fault tolerance. With an appropriate fault-tolerant control (FTC) strategy, dual three-phase SPMSM can achieve derated operation without the need for additional hardware support. However, in sensorless control mode, open-phase fault degrades the accuracy of rotor position estimation, thereby affecting the overall system performance. In response to this issue, this article proposes a robust sensorless control strategy that operates without the need for fault localization. The strategy demonstrates a capability for high-precision operation following a single open-phase fault ensuring that the steady-state performance of the drives is largely unaffected. First, the mechanism by which open-phase faults interfere with traditional back electromotive force (EMF) estimation methods is analyzed. Then, a robust sensorless strategy based on a dual extended state observer is proposed to enhance back-EMF estimation performance by adjusting the reference voltage in harmonic subspace. Without altering the motor model or the control structure, a novel harmonic subspace control framework is proposed. The proposed sensorless strategy eliminates the need for fault localization modules, not only mitigating the risk of misdiagnosis but also preventing performance degradation caused by diagnostic delays. Experimental results verify that the proposed sensorless strategy can achieve effective postfault operation without the need for fault localization or control reconfiguration.

item.title: Electrical Drives With Integrated Output Filters Part I—Converter Topologies, Filter Structures, and Design, Modulation, and System Integration
item.description: Electric motors consume over half of global electricity, yet most installations still operate as direct-on-line systems without variable-speed control. Broader adoption of variable speed drives has been limited by the installation complexity and the additional components required by pulsewidth modulation inverters, including shielded cables, inverter-duty motors, and external dv/dt and electromagnetic interference (EMI) filters. Recent advances in wide-bandgap (WBG) semiconductors enable high-frequency operation and compact power converters, but fast voltage transitions intensify dv/dt stress, common-mode excitation, cable-reflection overvoltages, EMI, and related reliability concerns. Drives with integrated output filters offer a unified drive-side solution to shape the high-frequency drive-machine interaction, enabling near-sinusoidal motor voltages, reduced losses and emissions, and the use of standard motors and unshielded cables. This facilitates large-scale retrofitting of existing installations with significant energy-saving potential. This article (Part I of II) presents a system-level review of drives with integrated output filters, focusing on converter topologies, output-filter structures and design considerations, and modulation strategies targeting dv/dt mitigation, common-mode reduction, and efficiency improvement. Key design considerations, including losses, voltage drop, component stress, and installation characteristics, are discussed, together with industrial practice, emerging trends, and implications for condition monitoring compatibility and process-level digitalization towards reliable and cost-effective WBG-based sine-out drives. Part II complements this review by covering observer and control strategies required for resonance stabilization and active damping in sinusoidal-output LC-filtered drives.

item.title: Stabilization of I–f Control via Instantaneous Power Regulation for Sensorless SPMSM Drives
item.description: The I–f control can be stabilized by adjusting the reference frequency and current magnitude via active and reactive power loops, respectively, extending its utility beyond the conventional startup phase of sensorless surface-mounted permanent magnet synchronous motor (SPMSM) drives. However, existing power-based methods lack theoretical tuning guidance and suffer from limited load capability. This article establishes a full-order analytical framework based on the proposed 7th- and 8th-order small-signal models. Root locus analysis reveals that system stability under the worst-case zero $d$-axis current condition is dominated by the integral term of the internal reactive power ($Q_{i}$) controller, with the proportional term providing auxiliary damping. A step-by-step parameter tuning method is proposed to ensure baseline stability and enhance load capability. To address inherent low-speed instability, a smooth deactivation method is developed. A dynamic $Q_{i}$ regulation strategy is introduced to prevent pole-slipping during zero-current deceleration. Comprehensive experiments on a 0.75 kW SPMSM validate that the proposed methodology withstands rated step loads, achieving stable operation across a wide speed range, including full-load acceleration and deceleration.

item.title: Predictive Current Control of H8-CSI-Fed High-Speed PMSM With Reduced Sensor Count and Low DC-Link Inductance
item.description: Current source inverters (CSIs) have attracted increasing attention for motor drive applications owing to their inherent short-circuit protection and motor-friendly characteristics. However, conventional CSI-fed drive systems typically require multiple sensors and a bulky DC-link inductance, hindering reliable and compact system designs. This article proposes a prediction-based coordinated control strategy for the front-end and rear-end stages of an H8-CSI-fed high-speed permanent magnet synchronous motor drive, enabling a compact CSI system that achieves reduced sensor count and low DC-link inductance without compromising the dynamic performance. For the rear-end CSI and motor control, the predictive current control and the rotor-position sensorless algorithm are implemented using only motor-current measurements, thereby eliminating both the capacitor-voltage and rotor-position sensors. In the front-end, multistep load-power prediction from the rear-end is incorporated into the current controller design to enable stable operation under low DC-link inductance. Experimental results verify that the proposed method maintains stable operation under a 10 A DC-link current with a 136 $\mu$H DC-link inductance, achieving $\boldsymbol{q}$-axis current step responses within three control steps at approximately 1 kHz electrical frequency. Comparative experiments against representative state-of-the-art multi-state-feedback CSI control methods further validate that the proposed method achieves faster current dynamic response with fewer sensors and a smaller DC-link inductance.

item.title: Turn-Off Oscillation Analysis of Parallel-Connected GaN Transistors
item.description: In high current power electronics applications, power transistors are often connected in parallel to enhance efficiency and achieve higher system power. When connecting power transistors in parallel resonant circuits can occur due to the parasitic parameters of the printed circuit board and the transistor itself. These resonant circuits cause oscillations, resulting in higher switching losses or even device damage. This article describes an approach to detect and suppress turn-off oscillations when connecting two gallium nitride (GaN) high-electron-mobility transistors in parallel. The model is formulated in state-space form, and the eigenvalues of the system matrix provide a pole-based stability criterion that distinguishes differential-mode oscillations between the paralleled devices from common-mode oscillations of the full half-bridge. Based on this approach, parameter maps are derived that relate system stability to the source inductances, the gate inductances, and the output capacitance of the transistors. The analytical predictions are verified by LTspice simulations with manufacturer models and double-pulse measurements on a dedicated hardware demonstrator. The results show that increasing source inductance strongly promotes differential-mode oscillations, while the gate inductance exhibits a finite range of values in which the system becomes unstable. Within this range, oscillations can occur even for perfectly symmetric gate inductances. The existence of a dedicated operating point further confirms that the output capacitance of the transistors and the DC-link inductance can cause common-mode oscillations.

item.title: An Innovative SVPWM Technique for Suppressing Circulating Currents and Doubling PWM Harmonic Frequency in Parallel Hybrid ANPC Inverter
item.description: High-power inverters utilized in clean energy systems such as wind power and photovoltaics are characterized by low switching frequencies, which can lead to challenges including reduced power density and inadequate output power quality. In response to the requirements of high-power power electronic systems, hybrid active neutral point clamped (HANPC) inverters and parallel inverters have emerged as a focal point in contemporary research and development efforts within the field of power electronics. This article combines a parallel three-level inverter with a hybrid ANPC three-level inverter to propose a parallel hybrid ANPC three-level (P-HANPCTL) inverter. This article examines various aspects of the inverter, including operational principles, neutral point (NP) potential control, circulating current suppression, switching frequency decoupling, and output line voltage PWM harmonic frequency doubling. The conditions needed for a space vector modulation (SVPWM) sequence to address these issues are summarized. Building upon these conditions, an integrated SVPWM approach for suppressing circulating current and doubling PWM harmonic frequency is proposed. This technique is designed for a P-HANPCTL inverter and includes NP potential control and switching frequency decoupling. Experimental outcomes validate the accuracy and efficacy of the proposed SVPWM approach.

item.title: Frequency Shift Filtering Based Impedance Measurement and Its Application to Field Wind Turbines
item.description: Field impedance measurement is an effective method for analyzing the stability of renewable energy grid-connection, especially for wind turbines. However, due to the fundamental frequency interference and background harmonic dynamics, the accuracy of existing measurement methods is extremely limited. To tackle these issues, a frequency shift filtering based impedance measurement technology is proposed, which enables accurate extraction of the impedance of field wind turbines. First, the topology and framework of the field wind turbine impedance measurement systems are introduced. By analyzing the voltage and current spectra of the measurement system, the effects of fundamental frequency spectral leakage and background harmonic dynamics on impedance measurement are emphasized. Then, a frequency shift filtering based impedance measurement topology is proposed. By designing a digital filter that can suppress interference signals above 2 Hz, a high-precision phasor extraction is achieved through frequency shift filtering. On this basis, an impedance measurement framework suitable for frequency coupling is built. Meanwhile, a dynamic harmonic impedance measurement method is studied to address the effect of background harmonic dynamics. To validate the performance of the proposed methods, simulations and field wind turbine tests are conducted. The results verify that the proposed methods achieve higher measurement accuracy than existing methods, with amplitude errors within 0.8 dB and phase errors of 4.9°.

item.title: A Piezoelectric-Resonator-Based “Active Inductor”
item.description: Piezoelectric resonators (PRs) have emerged as compelling alternative passive components for power conversion due to their high quality factors, planar form factors, and favorable scaling to small sizes. However, existing PR-based DC–DC converters typically require specialized topologies and complex multistate switching sequences, limiting their practicality and adoption. This article introduces a piezoelectric-resonator-based “active inductor” that directly emulates the dynamics of a magnetic inductor for use as a drag-and-drop replacement within conventional power converter architectures. By synchronizing a simple switching sequence to the PR’s mechanical resonant cycle, the proposed active inductor reproduces the fundamental voltage-current relationship of an inductor. Analytical models are developed to describe the effective inductance, amplitude of resonance, and efficiency of the active inductor, enabling design based on the resonator’s physical parameters. A predictive feedforward control strategy with voltage feedback is presented, enabling synchronization and high-efficiency operation without current sensing. Experimental validation in a buck converter demonstrates an effective inductance within 3% of the expected 4.26 mH and a peak converter efficiency of 96.9%. These results show that the proposed active inductor enables practical use of piezoelectric passive components in familiar power converter designs, offering a promising path toward magnetic-less, high-density power conversion.

item.title: Φ-SYNC: A Precurrent-Balancing Fast Phase-Adding Strategy for Multiphase VRMs in Data-Center Processors
item.description: Multiphase voltage regulator modules (VRMs) for high-current data-center processors commonly employ phase shedding to improve light-load efficiency. However, during step-up load transients from a phase-shedding state, conventional fast phase adding restores full-phase interleaving without actively compensating the large current gap between previously active and previously idle phases. This gap is then corrected only slowly by the current-sharing loop, which can increase the peak phase current and worsen the voltage undershoot. This article proposes a fast phase-adding strategy with precurrent balancing, termed phase synchronization (Φ-SYNC). When a step-up transient is detected while some phases are idle, Φ-SYNC temporarily overrides the idle-phase PWM/on-time commands and applies a controlled constant-on interval so that their inductor currents rapidly approach those of the previously active phases before returning to normal full-phase operation. If the transient ends early, a short residual compensation is completed in subsequent cycles. Φ-SYNC is implemented purely in firmware on a 16-phase VRM prototype and is evaluated against a baseline pulse-distribution-based current-mode constant-on-time scheme implementation and commercial controllers using the same power stage and printed circuit board (PCB) layout. Experiments under representative server-class transients show submicrosecond current equalization, reduced peak phase current, and improved undershoot without hardware modification. Additional 12-phase comparisons, expanded-condition tests, and a fixed-frequency digitally controlled VRM simulation further support its effectiveness and practical applicability.

item.title: A Two-Phase 140-A/1-MHz GaN–Silicon Hybrid Voltage Regulator Module for Vertical Power Delivery
item.description: This article presents a vertical power delivery (VPD) module that integrates hybrid devices within a compact 3-D structure. The proposed module addresses the limitations of individual device technologies by leveraging the fast switching capability of gallium nitride high electron mobility transistors (GaN HEMTs) and the high current handling capacity of Silicon mosfets. The VPD scheme minimizes power distribution network parasitics, enabling efficient high-frequency operation. Furthermore, an alloy powder inductor is optimized to achieve high peak current capability. Experimental results demonstrate that the two-phase prototype achieves a peak efficiency of 91.4% (1 V / 50 A) and full-load efficiency of 83.6% (1 V / 140 A) at 12 V input with a switching frequency of 1 MHz. The prototype current density reaches 0.79 A/mm$^{2}$ and an inductor current density of 2.75 A/mm$^{2}$.

item.title: Optimum Current Ripple Control With Inherent Mixed Conduction Mode to Improve Efficiency in Interleaved Totem-Pole PFC Converters
item.description: This article proposes an optimum current ripple (OCR) control strategy to improve interleaved totem-pole power factor correction (PFC) conversion efficiency over wide operating conditions. A generalized analytical formulation is derived to express instantaneous PFC losses as function of the inductor current ripple, which is selected as the primary control variable. An inherent mixed conduction mode (MCM) operation is obtained from the applied ripple profile, which is determined offline to minimize the PFC total losses, under given switching-frequency and peak-current constraints. A low processing implementation is performed in a standard microcontroller combining hysteresis current control and multidimensional look-up tables. Compared to other control methods, the proposed OCR-MCM shows significant efficiency improvements in a 7-kW three-channel interleaved PFC prototype, at different input/output voltages and loads. Optimal results are achieved in terms of power factor and current total harmonic distortion.

item.title: Power Electronics Converter Modeling and Solving Techniques for Real-Time Simulation: A Comprehensive Review and Modeling Workflow
item.description: There are numerous methodologies for addressing the modeling of power electronics converters (PECs) nowadays. Each of these approaches is closely related to the topology of the PEC as well as the intended application, and thus, developing a model for offline execution differs significantly from simulating one in real time (RT). To date, extensive research and significant advancements have been made in this field, resulting in the development of PEC models that are increasingly accurate, even for RT simulation. However, there are currently no established guidelines to follow regarding the modeling procedure for PECs based on their application and topology. This article aims to serve as a review of the current state of the art in PEC modeling by compiling the most relevant works and techniques and proposing a defined workflow for choosing an optimal modeling approach depending on the applications and requirements of the models. Moreover, it also enhances the importance of selecting an appropriate computational platform where the simulation of the model is conducted in order to establish a bidirectional relation between the simulation platform and the modeling approach and its solving method.

item.title: Isolated and Regulated Ultra-Flat DC–DC Power Converter for Extremely Wide Input Voltage Range (15 V–150 V), High Gain and Demanding Dynamics
item.description: This article proposes an isolated ultra-flat DC–DC converter architecture capable of directly converting high-voltage distribution rails (15–150 V) into regulated sub-1 V outputs with extremely high voltage conversion ratio. The solution is based on a resonant single-transformer structure specifically designed to enable large step-down operation while minimizing conduction path complexity. A 12:1 turns ratio with a single-turn secondary and reduced primary turns allows high gain realization using only one magnetic component and a minimized number of series devices along the main current path. The complete hardware implementation achieves a total height of 3.5 mm, making it compatible with surface power delivery and direct-to-chip integration constraints. An improved version incorporating a secondary-side active clamp is introduced to enhance controllability and transient behavior without increasing magnetic complexity. Both implementations are experimentally validated and quantitatively compared under equivalent operating conditions. The results demonstrate the feasibility of achieving extreme gain, wide gain variation, and ultra-low-profile integration using a single-magnetic isolated architecture suitable for future high-performance computing and AI processors.

item.title: Synergistic Paradigm for Second Harmonic Current Redistribution and Energy Optimization in Power Supply System via Time-Frequency Modeling
item.description: The utilization of harmonic energy and precise quantification of energy distribution represent critical challenges in advancing modern power supply system. This article presents a synergistic paradigm for dynamic second harmonic current redistribution and energy optimization in hybrid power supply system through time-frequency modeling approach. By introducing the adaptive masked Wigner–Ville distribution to the paradigm, the proposed method provides high-resolution time-frequency models in second harmonic current compensator to precisely capture harmonic behavior. The model guides dynamic current redistribution, balancing harmonic compensation with optimal energy usage through a multiobjective optimization strategy. Experimental validation demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed method in balancing harmonic compensation and energy efficiency. This article offers a novel synergistic paradigm for harmonic compensation and energy optimization, contributing a highly cost-effective and scalable solution to the advancement of hybrid power supply system.

item.title: Novel Current-Independent Capacitor Voltage Balancing Schemes for Modular Multilevel Converters
item.description: Modular multilevel converters (MMCs) are highly suitable for medium- and high-voltage DC–AC applications due to their modularity, scalability, and low harmonic content. A key challenge in MMCs is submodule capacitor voltage balancing (CVB), which is critical for ensuring safe, reliable, and efficient operation. Achieving CVB efficiently remains a significant research challenge. This article presents a novel CVB method for MMCs that does not require the arm current feedback signals. The proposed approach relies on the difference between the submodule capacitor voltage and the reference voltage, combined with a single proportional control loop per submodule, to achieve effective CVB. The proposed scheme yields reduced circulating currents as compared to existing methods. Additionally, an improved CVB scheme is introduced, which dynamically adjusts the controller gain to further suppress circulating currents. Simulation and experimental results validate the proposed methods, showcasing their improved performance in terms of reduced circulating current magnitude and capacitor voltage ripple when compared with conventional CVB strategies.

item.title: Transient Inductance in a High-Speed Axially Laminated SynRM: Parameter Sensitivity and Its Impact on Converter Characteristics
item.description: This article presents a comprehensive investigation into the transient inductance of a 27 kW, 100 000 rpm high-speed axially laminated anisotropic synchronous reluctance machine (ALASynRM). While traditional transversally laminated rotor synchronous reluctance machines exhibit significant angular dependence of transient inductance, this study reveals and theoretically quantifies the spatial invariance of this parameter in solid-rotor ALASynRMs due to high-frequency eddy current shielding in the conductive laminate layers. A refined finite element method (FEM) modeling approach is proposed that integrates 3-D end-winding leakage effects and material resistivity sensitivity to overcome the limitations of standard 2-D magnetic analysis. This modeling framework is rigorously validated through experimental measurements on a high-speed prototype, demonstrating a maximum deviation of 6.3% and an average deviation of only 2.5%. The article establishes a novel design-oriented theoretical framework that links the machine’s transient electromagnetic behavior directly to power converter performance. By quantifying the impact of transient inductance on current ripple and total harmonic distortion (THD), a systematic methodology for selecting optimal switching frequencies and DC-link voltages is provided. This approach ensures high-performance operation while accounting for the inherent computational constraints of high-speed motor controllers.

item.title: A Modular Coupled Inductor-Based Regenerative Cascaded Multicell Converter for Medium Voltage Drive
item.description: Cascaded multicell converter (CMC) is proved to be an effective solution for medium-voltage (MV) high-power variable-speed drives. To enable this converter with regeneration capability, the diode bridge rectifier is replaced by an active front-end rectifier (AFER) in each cell. However, this configuration requires large filter inductors and overrated transformers due to switching harmonics, produced by AFER. This article proposes a coupled-inductor-based modular regenerative CMC employing three-phase AFER cells. The modular design enhances scalability, while the coupled inductor (CI) effectively attenuates switching harmonics, thereby reducing transformer volt-ampere (VA) rating. In addition, the CI ensures equal current sharing among cells, reducing both control complexity and the number of current sensors required. The three-phase AFER eliminates subharmonic currents in motor and grid currents and reduces the DC-link capacitor requirement of each cell. The proposed topology is experimentally validated on a developed laboratory prototype, and the results confirm the effectiveness of the converter.

item.title: A Unidirectional Modular Magnetic-Coupled Converter (MMCC) With Reduced Switch Capacity for None-Regenerative Motor Drive
item.description: Although the conventional modular magnetic-coupled converter (MMCC)-based motor drive significantly improves power density, it suffers from high switch capacity. To address this issue, this article proposes a diode-based unidirectional MMCC, which reduces the capacity of fully-controlled switches by 39.5% compared with the conventional MMCC. Replacing switches with diodes complicates the DC capacitor voltage balancing principle and poses challenges to capacitance design. To solve these issues, the voltage balancing principle is revealed via the unique alternating conduction circuit model, without complex control strategies. Based on this principle, a dedicated DC capacitance design method is proposed, enabling the DC capacitance to be minimized even under zero/low-speed rated-torque operation. Moreover, system efficiency is improved by 0.3% due to the incorporated diodes. The feasibility of the proposed topology is verified via 4160-V 1-MVA simulations and 380-V 8-kVA experiments.

item.title: Second-Order Disturbance-Observer-Based Output-Feedback Voltage Control of DC/DC Converters Using Pole-Zero Cancellation
item.description: The proposed approach establishes an observer-based proportional-integral (PI)-type feedback system structure in which a second-order disturbance observer (SO-DOB) acts as a feed-forward compensator, thereby removing the requirement for the true values of converter parameters and load information. This work offers three main technical contributions. First, a pole-zero cancellation (PZC)-based observer is developed with a specially designed gain structure that diagonalizes the estimation error dynamics in a model-independent manner. Second, the SO-DOB enables robust estimation of disturbances induced by plant-model mismatch and load uncertainty, while simultaneously imposing prescribed second-order closed-loop dynamics. Third, a single-loop PI-type controller integrates the PZC-based observer and the SO-DOB to ensure exponential convergence of the regulation error and critically damped input? output behavior through PZC, without the use of current feedback. Experimental verification on a 3 kW bidirectional converter prototype confirms the practical effectiveness of the proposed controller and demonstrates a 29${\boldsymbol{\%}}$ performance improvement in comparison with a recent method.

item.title: Reconfigurable DAB Converter With Variable Transformer Turns for Wide Voltage Range Using Hybrid EPS Modulation
item.description: In this article, a variable transformer-based modified dual-active bridge (DAB) converter is proposed that has wide voltage range performance. The conventional DAB delivers maximum efficiency and performance only at unity voltage ratio and also fails to deliver wide voltage range operation. To overcome these limitations, this work proposes a modified DAB with reconfigurable secondary that can handle a wide output voltage range using transformer turns ratio. The variable secondary of the transformer provides three turns-ratio choices, and the reconfigurable bridge provides three operating modes for each. In effect, the converter operates in nine different modes, delivering higher performance over a voltage gain range of 0.3 to 4. In order to minimize the current stress across the switches and reduce losses, a hybrid extended phase shift modulation is proposed, which enhances the overall performance of the converter. A 500 W prototype is built for the proposed converter configuration, and the effectiveness is experimentally verified.

item.title: Fault Detection of Coil Misalignment in Multi-Receiver Wireless Power Transfer Systems With the Estimated Mutual Inductance
item.description: In a multi-receiver wireless power transfer (WPT) system, mutual inductance is a key determinant of electrical performance. In small mobile-device applications, receivers (RXs) can be placed or moved arbitrarily on a single transmitter (TX) pad, making coil misalignment unavoidable; therefore, reliable fault detection is essential for stable operation. This study proposes a two-stage approach to estimate the full set of mutual inductances. In Stage 1, each receiver is sequentially activated with a fixed pulse width modulation duty cycle to estimate the TX–RX mutual inductance MTi and equivalent load resistance Req,i. In Stage 2, receiver pairs are activated under the same condition to estimate the RX–RX mutual inductance Mik. Then, misalignment faults can be detected by comparing the estimated mutual inductance values with predefined thresholds. A three-receiver prototype (10 mm airgap) validates accurate mutual inductance estimation and reliable fault detection.

item.title: Adaptive Virtual Impedance Control for Series Active Compensator to Improve PV Power Injection in Distribution Networks
item.description: With the increase of photovoltaic (PV) penetration in distribution networks (DNs), the overvoltage issue caused by reverse-active power and the high R/X ratio has resulted in serious PV curtailment, which has been an important challenge for the development of renewable energy. To overcome the above issue, this article proposes an adaptive virtual impedance control method based on series active compensators (SACs). The overvoltage issue is effectively mitigated, and the power injection capability of PV systems is improved. By using SACs, the equivalent R/X ratio of DNs at the fundamental frequency is reshaped to achieve dynamic voltage regulation. Compared with other compensation methods, the proposed method has a lower device capacity by constructing optimization equations for apparent power and output voltage based on virtual impedance. And the loss of PV power in feeder is reduced. The relationship between the R/X ratio and overvoltage is analyzed, and its safety threshold for solving overvoltage is obtained. The simulation and experimental results verify the effectiveness and correctness of the proposed method.

item.title: A Wearable Footstep Energy Harvester With Novel Dual-Clutch Mechanical Motion Rectification for Self-Powered Sensing
item.description: Wearable and autonomous sensing systems require efficient energy conversion under low-frequency, bidirectional mechanical excitations generated by daily human motion. This work presents a novel dual-clutch ratchet energy harvester (DREH) that converts bidirectional heel motions into unidirectional high-speed rotation, enabling direct DC power generation without conventional AC–DC rectification losses. The dual-clutch architecture ensures robust motion rectification under weak excitation and enables recovery of elastic potential energy during the liftoff phase, thereby improving effective energy utilization. A coupled dynamic–electromechanical model is developed to analyze the system behavior and predict electrical output. A compact prototype (86.4 cm3, 89 g) is fabricated and experimentally evaluated under pseudowalk and natural walking conditions. Experimental results show that elastic energy recovery increases output power by 59.5% at 0.3 Hz; at 6 km/h with a 75 $\boldsymbol{\Omega}$ load, the prototype delivers 82 mW peak and 28 mW average power with a driving force below 14 N. System-level validation demonstrates continuous operation of a wireless sensing node, confirming the DREH as an effective self-sustained power source for wearable and industrial sensing applications.

item.title: An Active-Soft-Switching DC Transformer With Auxiliary Converter for DC Offshore Wind Turbine
item.description: Over the past decade, offshore wind farms have gained widespread attention from scholars and industries. In response to the trend of locating wind farms further away from shore with a larger installation scale, an all-DC system is proposed to connect the offshore wind turbines and onshore substations, featuring no reactive power or synchronism requirement. The article proposes an active soft-switching DC transformer (AS2-DCT) topology with a small auxiliary converter for a DC wind turbine interface application. In the topology, the main converter’s current can be actively reshaped by the auxiliary converter, enabling the full-range soft-switching operation of the main converter. Compared with conventional single-active-bridge (SAB) topology, the AS2-DCT achieves quasizero-current switching (QZCS) of input H-bridge switches. Besides, the AC side current is actively reshaped into a trapezoidal waveform instead of the triangular waveform in SAB or the sine waveform in LLC, reducing current stress. The feasibility and effectiveness of this proposed topology have been verified through a 13.6 MW simulation model and a 1 kW scale-down prototype.

item.title: Adaptive Quantum-Based Least Mean Fourth Control for Multisource Isolated Three-Phase Microgrids: Experimental Analysis and Performance Evaluation
item.description: This article presents an adaptive quantum normalized least-mean fourth (AQ-LMF) filtering control strategy to improve power quality (PQ) in standalone microgrids (MGs). Integrated with a voltage source converter (VSC), the controller provides fast dynamic response, enhanced stability, DC-offset rejection, reduced steady-state error, and minimized oscillations, while ensuring frequency regulation, load balancing, and harmonic mitigation under highly distorted loads. The algorithm employs error-correlation energy and signal normalization to accelerate convergence, reduce computational burden, and maintain stability at higher step sizes. A solar photovoltaic (PV) system is interfaced to the DC link through a boost converter using an incremental conductance (INC) maximum power point tracking method, while an energy storage system (ESS) connected via a bidirectional DC–DC converter balances power among solar, wind, and load demand during generation variability and load fluctuations. The proposed estimator reaches its steady-state tolerance band within two update cycles, with subsequent iterations confined within noise and quantization limits. Despite a load current total harmonic distortion (THD) of 29.61%, the AQ-LMF control limits supply current THD to 4.11%, complying with the IEEE-519 (<5%) standard. Experimental validation under dynamic conditions confirms the robustness and effectiveness of the proposed approach for reliable standalone MG operation.

item.title: Kinetic Energy Based Power Smoothing Method for High-Inertia Wind Turbines Using ESO-MFPCC
item.description: Large capacity wind turbines have the characteristic of high inertia, which further provides conditions for leveraging the stored kinetic energy to regulate and smooth the power output. However, the high inertia will make it difficult to tune the proportional-integral (PI) parameters of the machine side control link and challenge the transient behavior and responsiveness of the control strategy. To stabilize output power and achieve dynamic performance improvement, this article proposes a kinetic energy based power smoothing method for high-inertia wind turbines using model-free predictive current control based on extended state observer (ESO-MFPCC). By cascading a second order filter (SOF) in the active power control loop, the output power fluctuation of the wind turbine is reduced effectively. The ESO-MFPCC scheme eliminates the dependence on system parameters, thereby solving the PI controller tuning problem and enhancing the dynamic responsiveness of high-inertia wind turbines. Finally, both simulation and experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method effectively smooths the output power: in the 5 min stochastic complex wind-speed simulation, the mean power variation rate is reduced by approximately 50%. Moreover, in the 15 s step-wind simulation, the phase-A current total harmonic distortion is 1.35%, indicating a low harmonic distortion level.

item.title: Reserved-Energy-Based Control Strategy for Enhanced Load Transient Response in Low-Capacitance Solid-State Transformers
item.description: Conventional solid-state transformer (SST) architectures based on the cascaded H-bridge converter typically require large high-voltage side capacitors to suppress low-frequency voltage ripples. These capacitors are further stressed during load transients, complicating efforts to reduce their capacitance. Large capacitor banks increase system footprint and reduce reliability, especially with high-power-density electrolytic capacitors. The capacitors absorb transient power imbalance between the input and output ports of an SST. Conventional control strategies often lead to uneven distribution of transient energy, placing disproportionate stress on certain capacitors and resulting in oversized capacitance requirements. To address these challenges, this article proposes a reserve-energy-aided control strategy for effective energy distribution across DC-link capacitors in low-capacitance SSTs. The proposed solution is validated using a 1-kVA, 230-V/250-V, 50-kHz single-phase SST prototype, demonstrating improved transient response and operational stability under varying load conditions.

item.title: Comprehensive Analysis of an Isolated Boost Converter Based on the Converter PWM Switch (CPS) Concept
item.description: A new pulse width modulation (PWM) switch concept, referred to as the converter PWM switch (CPS), has recently been introduced in the literature. Unlike traditional semiconductor switches, the CPS employs a power converter as a controllable PWM switch while maintaining the power-transfer capability. By replacing one of the semiconductor switches in a traditional boost converter with an isolated CPS, a new CPS-based isolated boost converter (CPS-IBC) is created, which can achieve zero voltage switching (ZVS), a wide voltage conversion range and high efficiency. This article presents the first comprehensive analysis of the ZVS conditions for the proposed CPS-IBC and introduces a rms current estimation method, both of which enhance the understanding and practical implementation of CPS-based converters. Building upon these analyses, an improved modulation scheme is proposed to reduce conduction losses and further enhance the overall efficiency of the CPS-IBC. A 10 kW CPS-IBC prototype is developed to validate the topology and demonstrate the benefits of the proposed modulation. The experimental results highlight the strong potential of the CPS-IBC for high-performance isolated power conversion applications.

item.title: Generic and Flexible Digital Model of DAB Converters With Various Topologies and Control for Efficient Optimal Design
item.description: To evaluate the performance of dual-active-bridge (DAB) converters across various topologies and control schemes for optimal design, this article proposes a generic explicit digital model applicable two-level (2L)/three-level (3L) half-bridge (HB), full-bridge (FB), and three-phase (3P) topologies with a unified control structure. Voltage and current expressions for a single bridge leg considering both 2L and 3L topologies are developed in a generalized manner, and thus the model of DAB topologies with different number of legs can be constructed by superimposing the corresponding number of individual bridge leg models. Subsequently, the digital model, i.e., discrete-time model of DAB converters with different topologies and control configurations, is derived based on the circuit differential equations and a unified closed-loop control system by applying backward Euler method. Therefore, both steady-state and dynamic performance of DAB converters can be predicted in the proposed model. Owing to the analytical formulation of operating parameters and generic expressions for different topologies and control, the calculation speed of the proposed digital model can be accelerated compared to commercial simulation platforms such as MATLAB/Simulink and PLECS, and the design efficiency can be significantly enhanced, especially when it eliminates the need for frequent manual adjustments of topologies, modulation, and loss-thermal models of power devices. Simulation and experimental tests validate that the digital DAB model can achieve high accuracy under various topologies with fast execution speed.

item.title: Dual-Mode Seamless Transition for Hybrid Distribution Transformer With Energy Storage
item.description: This article proposes a dual-mode seamless transition control scheme for the hybrid distribution transformer with energy storage (HDT-ES) system, explicitly addressing the actuation delays of mechanical circuit breakers. First, a phased transition strategy is developed based on real-time state monitoring. By leveraging the series converter for transient voltage compensation, it ensures continuous power supply reliability during the switching process. Second, a dual-mode control framework is established to coordinate the shunt and series converters. This framework ensures stable control authority handover between grid-connected and islanded modes. Third, a coordinated DC-link voltage control strategy is designed to manage the power balance between the converters and the energy storage unit during different operating modes. Simulation and experimental results validate the effectiveness and stability of the proposed strategy under various load conditions.

item.title: Improvement of Overload Capability and Torque Density for PMVM With MMF Reconstruction via Stator Flux Barriers
item.description: Permanent magnet vernier machines (PMVMs) can utilize multiple stator magneto-motive force (MMF) components with different pole-pairs to contribute to energy conversion, offering the advantage of high torque density. However, the low-pole-pair stator MMF components would generate low-pole-pair no-working flux density harmonics, which lead to the poor overload capability in conventional multiple-working-harmonic (MWH) PMVMs. This article proposes a novel PMVM with strategically designed stator flux barriers. Under the unique design, the stator MMF components are reconstructed, where the low-pole-pair MMF components are suppressed, while the high-pole-pair MMF components are enhanced. As a result, both the improved overload capacity and high torque density can be achieved. Specifically, an equivalent magnetic circuit model is established to analyze the effect of stator flux barriers. Furthermore, the comprehensive performance comparisons between the proposed and conventional PMVMs are conducted by finite element analysis (FEA). The results demonstrate that the proposed PMVM achieves the torque improvements of 50.5% under rated-load and good torque performance under five-times overload conditions. Meanwhile, the cogging torque is reduced. Finally, a prototype is manufactured and tested to verify the performance advantages.

item.title: Junction Temperature-Based Adaptive Short Circuit Detection Technique for SiC MOSFETs
item.description: Silicon carbide (SiC) MOSFETs have a low short-circuit (SC) withstand capacity. Hence, an SC detection circuit with a low SC detection time ($t_{SCD}$) and high robustness is required to achieve an effective SC protection for SiC MOSFETs. To achieve both the objectives simultaneously, mostly two-stage SC detection techniques are suggested in the literature. The primary stage in these techniques is designed to have a very low $t_{SCD}$. However, a few of the suggested primary stage are known to have a low robustness while the others are known to be incapable of detecting a fault under load (FUL) SC condition. To improve the overall robustness and to identify FUL, a desaturation (DESAT)-based SC detection technique is usually used as a secondary stage. In a DESAT-based technique, the reference voltage ($V_\text{REF}$) for SC detection is kept based on the power device output characteristic and its worst-case operating junction temperature ($T_{J}$). However, this leads to a suboptimal $t_{SCD}$ as the device may not be operating at its worst-case $T_{J}$ preceeding an SC event. Thereby, this may adversely affect the SC protection effectiveness by making the secondary stage slower. To address the aforementioned challenge, this manuscript proposes a novel technique to adaptively vary ${V}_{REF}$ based on the feedback of $T_{J}$ to achieve an optimal $t_{SCD}$. Further, the mathematical formulation for the rate at which $V_{REF}$ should be varied and operational constraints necessary to mitigate a misdetection during normal operation are also determined. Experimental investigation of the proposed technique is carried out by conducting SC at 800 V on a 1.2 kV rated SiC MOSFET. Results show up to 24.3$\%$ reduction in $t_{SCD}$ compared with the existing secondary protection technique.

item.title: Zero-Shot Open Circuit Fault Diagnosis of Converter Based on Prior-Knowledge Injected Dual Bayesian Network With Attention Mechanism
item.description: Power electronic systems serve as core infrastructure for modern energy conversion and power control. Their reliability is crucial for the stable operation of key fields, such as industrial power systems, transportation, and aerospace. Open-circuit faults are difficult to detect, which can lead to serious consequences. While effective in data-rich environments, existing data-driven approaches’ reliance on extensive labeled data hinders their practical deployment. The reason is that acquiring comprehensive fault data in real-world settings is often prohibitively expensive. To address this, this article proposes a dual Bayesian zero-shot fault diagnosis approach based on prior-knowledge injected with attention mechanism (PKIDBAAM). This approach constructs a fault attribute space with clear physical meaning by analyzing the physical relationship between the Vienna rectifier topology and fault modes. It employs a multihead attention mechanism to dynamically fuse multidomain fault features from three-phase current signals. A dual Bayesian inference framework combining naive Bayes and integrated multiple Gaussian Bayesian algorithms is designed to achieve high accuracy recognition of inaccessible open-circuit faults. The verification results on a Vienna rectifier experimental platform show that it significantly outperforms conventional classical machine learning models, which provides a new solution for intelligent fault diagnosis in power electronic systems.

item.title: A 124 $\mu$W Inductive Sensing SoC With Force and Position Detection for Virtual Buttons
item.description: This article presents a 4-channel, ultra low-power, phase-based inductive sensing system-on-chip (SoC) for force-sensitive virtual buttons in portable devices. The solution addresses key challenges in human-machine interface (HMI) design, including sub-micron displacement sensitivity, resilience to electromagnetic interference (EMI), and low-power always-on operation. A novel active-drive, phase detector architecture supports programmable drive frequencies up to 30 MHz, while a low-amplitude transmitter (only 10 mV rms across the sensor) minimizes EMI emissions. The SoC measures inductance changes as small as a few hundred ppm, even with low-Quality(Q)-Factor sensors (Q $\boldsymbol{\geq}$ 5). On-chip digital postprocessing algorithms provide real-time baseline drift compensation, Q-factor scaling, and calibration, ensuring robustness across different conditions. The design was fabricated in GlobalFoundries 55 nm CMOS process with extensive silicon validation, including process corner-lot characterization, high-temperature operating life (HTOL) conditions, and real-world user interactions. The SoC achieves 0.1 µm deflection resolution while consuming 124 µW at a 100 Hz scan rate. A phone form-factor prototype integrating the SoC and sensor demonstrates reliable detection of four distinct force levels and spatial press positions (to 1 mm resolution). To our knowledge, this work presents the first comprehensive demonstration of an inductive virtual button platform combining high-resolution sensing, ultra-low power consumption, robust postprocessing, and multilevel force/position detection for portable device applications.

item.title: Compact Temperature and Static Pressure Compensation System for Differential Pressure Sensor Based on Neural Network and Improved Wolf Algorithm
item.description: For piezoresistive pressure sensor, sensing performance is typically ensured by compensating primarily for the temperature-induced drift. However, for high-precision differential pressure measurements in high static pressure scenarios, the measurement deviation caused by the static pressure cannot be ignored. Therefore, this study proposed a compact two-parameter compensation system for differential pressure sensors. First, a novel structure was proposed for synchronous acquisition of static pressure, temperature, and differential pressure. In addition, a two-layer microcontroller unit (MCU) compensation hardware was designed considering the nonlinear errors caused by temperature and static pressure, which ensures acquisition accuracy through 16-bit analog-to-digital (AD) and digital-to-analog (DA) converter circuits. Furthermore, a back propagation (BP) neural network based on the improved grey wolf optimal algorithm was employed to model the coupling relationship between temperature, static pressure, and difference pressure, thereby overcoming the limitations of polynomial fitting and achieving high-precision difference pressure sensing under multitemperature and high-static pressure. Calibration experiments were conducted to validate the proposed system, and the results compared with those of typical compensation methods. The maximum error of the compensated differential pressure sensor within the temperature range of −40 to 80 $ {}^{\boldsymbol{\circ}} $C and static pressure range of 0-30 MPa was within 0.28%FS (% of full scale), demonstrating that the proposed system significantly reduced the error influence caused by static pressure.

item.title: Seamless Grid-Connected/Islanded Transition in Fully Grid-Forming PV Powered Microgrids
item.description: This paper investigates the full-state virtual oscillator control (fVOC) method to realize the flexible operation of 100% PV-powered microgrid. In the grid-connected mode, the enhanced DC voltage stability of fVOC enables the grid-forming PVs to provide the dynamic support while being compatible with the maximum power point tracking function. This dual capability is critical to replace the grid-following operation under the very high penetration of renewable sources. In the islanded situation, the reconnection of the microgrid to the bulk grid leads to large phase jumps, which can trigger the overcurrent saturation and induce the DC voltage instability in grid-forming PVs. To address this issue, a phase adaption current limiting method in fVOC is proposed. The full-order system modeling is performed to guide the parameter design of the proposed method. The Lyapunov function is derived to reveal the enhanced transient stability of the grid-forming PV system during the reconnection of the islanded microgrid. The superiority of the proposed method is verified in both simulations and field tests in a 100% PV powered microgrid. The mode transition between grid-connected and islanded is seamless without islanding detection and pre-synchronization.

item.title: Renewable Scenario Generation Using Quantum Generative Adversarial Networks
item.description: With the increasing penetration of renewable resources in modern power systems, scenario generation for renewable energy has emerged as a critical tool for system operation and planning. Among the widely studied methods, Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) are popular. Despite its model-free nature, it suffers from high computational demands due to its extensive trainable parameters and often struggles to capture intricate data patterns. To address these challenges, we employ quantum computing techniques that harness quantum entanglement principles. We propose, for the first time, a method of generating a quantum-enhanced renewable energy scenario based on a hybrid quantum GANs (QGANs) architecture. Specifically, given historical data of renewable resources, we design a quantum generator using parameterized quantum circuits. This quantum neural network achieves superior expressivity compared to its classical counterparts while requiring significantly fewer trainable parameters. Then, the resulting QGANs architecture combines this quantum generator with a classical discriminator for the effective generation of renewable energy scenarios. Quantum measurements also inherently introduce randomness into the generated renewable scenarios. The simulation results verify the rationale of the proposed method and demonstrate its effectiveness in capturing the spatio-temporal characteristics of renewable resources.

item.title: Central Controller for Photovoltaic Power Plants With Hybrid Energy Storage Systems Providing Automatic Frequency Restoration Reserve
item.description: Large-scale photovoltaic (PV) power plants have been increasingly used in ancillary service markets, providing services at significantly different time scales. These plants require additional flexibility to provide different services simultaneously and the solution is often sought in application of hybrid energy storage systems (HESSs). In HESSs, the power demand is shared between the storage units to maximise their performance and lifetime. However, this requires a detailed model of all storage elements that must be taken into account by the central controller of the PV plant. This aspect has not been yet studied in detail in the literature. In this paper, a central controller is proposed for a PV power plant with a HESS. This controller allows the PV plant to participate simultaneously in the day-ahead and the secondary reserve markets, providing both energy and power reserve services. First, the assets are scheduled in an optimal way, considering a horizon of 24 hours and taking into consideration weather forecasts and the expected balancing energy requests. Then, a short-term rolling-horizon optimisation with a time horizon of 30 minutes is used to consider the real operating conditions of the PV power plant and state of the storage units. The efficiency of each of the storage elements is modelled in detail for the short-term optimisation.
